SOURCE: "UNITER: UNiversal Image-TExt Representation Learning", Yen-Chun Chen, Linjie Li, Licheng Yu et al. (Microsoft Dynamics 365 AI Research). ECCV 2020; the file is arXiv:1909.11740v3 (17 Jul 2020).
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/08-multimodal-engineering/sources/chen-2020-uniter.pdf

COVERAGE: I read all 67,290 chars (that count includes the page markers I added), covering all 26 pages including appendices A.1–A.8. I skimmed the references. I did not run the captions script and took captions from the text.

CLAIMS
- claim: UNITER is single-stream. Detector regions and word tokens go into one Transformer together. Each region's input is its Faster R-CNN pooled ROI feature plus a 7-d box vector, each passed through an FC layer, then summed and normalised.
  number: 7-d location vector; base model 86M parameters, large 303M
  setup: Faster R-CNN pretrained on VG objects and attributes (Anderson 2018 features)
  quote: "we ﬁrst use Faster R-CNN 2 to extract the visual features (pooled ROI features) for each region. We also encode the location features for each region via a 7-dimensional vector." (p.4). "with much fewer parameters (UNITER-base: 86M, LXMERT: 183M, VilBERT: 221M)" (p.11)
- claim: In-domain pretraining data beats out-of-domain data even though out-of-domain has more images. Using both gives the best result.
  number: Meta-Sum 400.93 (COCO+VG) vs 396.91 (CC+SBU) vs 405.24 (both). COCO+VG gives 5.6M training pairs; CC is 3.0M pairs and SBU 990K.
  setup: UNITER-base, all tasks, Table 2 rows 11, 13 and 14. Meta-Sum adds VQA, Flickr IR and TR, NLVR2 and RefCOCO+.
  quote: "A performance drop (396.91 in L13) from the model trained on In-domain data (COCO + Visual Genome) (400.93 in L11)" … "With doubled data size, the model continues to improve (405.24 in L14)." (pp.10–11)
- claim: Ablation of pretraining tasks. MLM and ITM matter most. MRC-kl is the best MRM variant, and it adds to MRFR. WRA helps mainly region-level tasks (VQA, RefCOCO+).
  number: Meta-Sum 314.34 (no pretraining), 346.24 (text-only BERT), 393.04 (MLM+ITM), 397.09 (+MRC-kl), 399.97 (+MRFR), 400.93 (+WRA). MRFR alone gives 344.66.
  setup: UNITER-base, in-domain data, Table 2
  quote: "MRC-kl (L9) achieves the best performance (397.09) when combined with MLM + ITM, while MRC (L7) the worst (393.97)" (p.10)
- claim: Conditional masking (mask one modality while the other stays whole) beats joint random masking.
  number: Meta-Sum 399.97 vs 396.51
  setup: UNITER-base, in-domain data, MLM+ITM+MRC-kl+MRFR
  quote: "w/o conditional masking (L12), we observe a decrease in Meta-Sum score (396.51) compared to that with conditional masking (399.97)" (p.10)
- claim: Headline results set a new state of the art. On VQA the large model beats LXMERT, but the base model does not.
  number: VQA test-std 72.91 (base) and 74.02 (large) vs LXMERT 72.54. NLVR2 test-P 77.85 and 79.98 vs LXMERT 74.50. Flickr IR R@1 72.52 and 75.56; zero-shot Flickr IR R@1 66.16 and 68.74.
  setup: pretrained on in-domain plus out-of-domain data. VQA training adds VG question-answer pairs. NLVR2 uses the Pair-biattn head. Retrieval finetuning uses hard negatives.
  quote: "UNITER-base model also outperforms the others by a large margin across all tasks except VQA" (p.11)
- claim: Within the same model, WRA gives its biggest gain on zero-shot retrieval.
  number: zero-shot Flickr TR R@1 77.50 → 83.60; zero-shot IR R@1 65.82 → 68.74
  setup: UNITER-large, both data sources, Table 8
  quote: "We observe large performance gains in zero-shot setup for image/text retrieval and consistent gains across all other tasks." (p.23)

LIMITS:
- No inference latency or detector cost is reported anywhere. The only compute figure is for pretraining: "882 and 3645 V100 GPU hours" for base and large (p.8).
- The paper never says how many regions it takes per image.
- The authors admit the detector features are contaminated for referring-expression tasks: "we ignore this issue and use the same features [2] as the others" (p.21). They say the features lift MAttNet by 1.5%.
- Future work they name is interaction "between raw image pixels and sentence tokens" (p.14). That marks the detector bottleneck that CLIP, ViT and LLaVA later removed.
- Retrieval is a cross-encoder: every image-text pair is scored jointly through [CLS]. The cost of this at retrieval time is not discussed.
- All results are finetuned. The only zero-shot result is Flickr retrieval.
- MRC labels come from the detector itself, not ground truth.

BUILDS ON: BERT (Devlin et al., NAACL 2019); Transformer (Vaswani et al., NeurIPS 2017); bottom-up/top-down Faster R-CNN features (Anderson et al., CVPR 2018); the two-stream ViLBERT (Lu et al., NeurIPS 2019) and LXMERT (Tan & Bansal, EMNLP 2019); single-stream VisualBERT (Li et al., arXiv 2019), VL-BERT (Su et al., ICLR 2020), Unicoder-VL (Li et al., AAAI 2020) and B2T2 (Alberti et al., EMNLP 2019); IPOT (Xie et al., arXiv 2018); optimal transport (Peyré & Cuturi, 2019); knowledge distillation for MRC-kl (Hinton et al., 2015).

FIGURES:
- Fig. 1 (p.2): "Overview of the proposed UNITER model … consisting of an Image Embedder, a Text Embedder and a multi-layer Transformer, learned through four pre-training tasks". It shows R-CNN features plus location going into one stream with tokens, which is quicker to grasp than the prose.
- Fig. 5 (p.22, the conditional vs joint masking dog example) is a backup choice.

PROBLEMS:
- The table text extracted in a usable form, but header alignment was lost.
- Appendix A.3 cites "Table 2 (row 10 & 11)" for conditional masking, but the actual comparison is rows 10 vs 12. This inconsistency is in the source itself.
- No embedded instructions were found.
